title: Building sentences
goal: Build and ask simple present-tense sentences about your life, your likes, and what you can, want or have to do.

grammar.p: Spanish usually goes subject + verb + rest, and you often drop the subject pronoun because the verb ending already tells you who: *Trabajo en el hospital* = I work at the hospital. In questions, put the question word first, then the verb: *¿Dónde trabajas?* Question words always carry an accent: *qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cómo, cuánto, cuál, por qué*. Yes/no questions keep normal order and just change intonation: *¿Tienes hijos?*
ex: ¿Dónde vives?
Where do you live?
¿A qué hora empieza la clase?
What time does the class start?
¿Tienes hijos?
Do you have kids?

grammar.p: Put *no* right before the verb: *No trabajo hoy.* Spanish uses double negatives: if *nada*, *nadie* or *nunca* comes after the verb, you still need *no* before it (*No quiero nada*). If *nunca* or *nadie* comes first, drop the *no* (*Nunca como carne. Nadie viene.*). Never say *nunca no*.
ex: No quiero nada.
I don't want anything.
Nunca como carne. / No como carne nunca.
I never eat meat.
Nadie quiere trabajar el domingo.
Nobody wants to work on Sunday.

grammar.h: Connectors: y, pero, porque, entonces, también, tampoco
grammar.p: *y* (and), *pero* (but), *porque* (because — one word, no accent), *entonces* (so / then), *también* (also, too), *tampoco* (not either). Use *también* to agree with a positive statement and *tampoco* with a negative one. Don't confuse *porque* (because) with *¿por qué?* (why?).
ex: No puedo ir porque tengo que trabajar.
I can't go because I have to work.
Llueve mucho, entonces no salgo.
It's raining a lot, so I'm not going out.
Yo no fumo y mi esposa tampoco.
I don't smoke and neither does my wife.

grammar.h: The gustar pattern (gustar, encantar, doler, importar)
grammar.p: With *gustar*, the thing you like is the subject, and the person goes in front as *me, te, le, nos, les*. Use *gusta* with one thing or an activity (infinitive) and *gustan* with plural things. *Encantar* (to love), *doler* (to hurt) and *importar* (to matter / to mind) work the same way. Add *a mí, a ti, a mi papá…* for emphasis or clarity. To agree: *A mí también* (me too) / *A mí tampoco* (me neither).
ex: Me gusta el café, pero no me gustan los dulces.
I like coffee, but I don't like sweets.
A mi papá le duelen las rodillas.
My dad's knees hurt.
¿Te importa si abro la ventana?
Do you mind if I open the window?

grammar.p: Many verbs change their stem vowel in every form except *nosotros*: e→ie (*querer → quiero*, *empezar → empieza*, *preferir → prefiero*), o→ue (*poder → puedo*, *dormir → duermo*, *volver → vuelvo*), u→ue (*jugar → juego*), e→i (*pedir → pido*). To say what you want, can, or have to do, conjugate the first verb and leave the second as an infinitive: *quiero comer*, *puedo ir*, *tengo que trabajar*.
ex: Nosotros pedimos tacos y ellos piden enchiladas.
We order tacos and they order enchiladas.
¿Puedes venir mañana?
Can you come tomorrow?
Tengo que llamar a mi mamá.
I have to call my mom.

phrases: How do you say … in Spanish?
I don't like it at all.
What do you want to do?

items.why: The thing liked (los tacos) is plural → gustan.
Where = dónde (with an accent in questions).

items.q: Mi hermano ___ ocho horas todas las noches.
items.qen: My brother sleeps eight hours every night.
items.why: dormir is o→ue; él → duerme.
After no + verb, 'anyone' (a person) = nadie. Spanish uses the double negative.

items.qen: She has to work on Saturday.
items.why: 'Has to' = tener que + infinitive; ella → tiene que.

items.q: A mi papá le ___ la espalda.
items.why: doler works like gustar; la espalda is singular → duele.

items.q: How do you say: "I don't like coffee either."
opts: A mí también me gusta el café.
A mí tampoco me gusta el café.
A mí tampoco me gustan el café.
items.why: Negative agreement → tampoco; gustar pattern with a singular thing → me gusta el café.

items.q: Your friend says: "Me encanta la música mexicana." You love it too. Best reply?
items.why: Agreeing with a positive gustar/encantar statement → A mí también.

items.q: Your friend says: "No me gusta correr." You don't like it either. Best reply?
items.why: Agreeing with a negative statement → tampoco; with gustar it's A mí tampoco.

items.qen: How much does the appointment cost?
items.why: 'How much' with a verb (cuesta) = cuánto.

items.q: No puedo ir ___ tengo que trabajar.
items.qen: I can't go because I have to work.
items.why: Because = porque (one word, no accent).

items.q: Mi carro no funciona, ___ tomo el autobús.
items.qen: My car doesn't work, so I take the bus.
items.why: 'So' introducing a result = entonces.

items.qen: Can you play soccer on Saturday?
items.why: poder is o→ue; tú → puedes.

items.qen: We always order the same food.
items.why: Stem changes skip nosotros: pedir → pedimos.

items.qen: Do you all like to dance?
items.why: The thing liked is an activity (infinitive) → always gusta, even if the people are plural.
Either 'Nunca como carne' or 'No como carne nunca'. Never put no and nunca together before the verb.

items.q: Mis hijos ___ jugar en el parque.
items.qen: My kids want to play in the park.
items.why: querer is e→ie; ellos → quieren.

items.q: —¿Por qué no vienes? —___ tengo que trabajar.
items.qen: —Why aren't you coming? —Because I have to work.
items.why: The answer 'because' is porque: one word, no accent.

items.q: How do you say: "What time does the class start?"
items.why: 'At what time' = ¿A qué hora…?; empezar is e→ie → empieza.

items.qen: Do you mind if I open the window?
items.why: importar works like gustar; the thing that matters is 'if I open the window' (singular idea) → importa.

items.en: I sleep eight hours every night.
items.why: dormir is o→ue; yo → duermo.

items.en: Do you prefer coffee or tea?
items.why: preferir is e→ie; tú → prefieres.

items.en: Why don't you eat meat?
items.why: The question 'why' = por qué: two words, accent on qué.

items.en: My knees hurt.
items.why: doler works like gustar; las rodillas is plural → duelen.

items.en: It's raining a lot, so I'm not going out.
items.why: 'So' introducing a result = entonces (así que and por eso also work).

items.en: What's your sister's name?
items.why: Spanish asks 'How is she called?' → ¿Cómo se llama?

items.en: I don't want anything.
items.why: no + verb + nada = not … anything.

items.en: My wife never goes to the gym.
items.why: nunca before the verb, with no 'no' (jamás also works).

items.q: Yo no hablo francés, y mi hermano ___.
items.en: I don't speak French, and neither does my brother.
items.why: Agreeing with a negative → tampoco.

items.en: They love soccer.
items.why: encantar works like gustar; el fútbol is singular → encanta.

items.q: Yo ___ que llamar a mi mamá.
items.en: I have to call my mom.
items.why: tener que + infinitive; yo → tengo.

items.en: You all always order tacos al pastor.
items.why: pedir is e→i; ustedes → piden.

items.en: Where do you work?
items.why: Where = dónde, with an accent in questions.

items.en: My son wants to be a doctor.
items.why: querer is e→ie; él → quiere + infinitive.

items.en: How many children do you have?
items.why: usted uses the él/ella form → tiene.

items.en: I don't know the answer.
items.why: saber is irregular in the yo form: sé (with an accent).

items.en: What time do you get back home?
items.why: volver is o→ue; tú → vuelves.

items.q: Me gusta el café, ___ no me gusta el té.
items.en: I like coffee, but I don't like tea.
items.why: But = pero.

items.en: On Sundays my kids play soccer.
items.why: jugar is u→ue; ellos → juegan.

items.en: Does your head hurt?
items.why: doler works like gustar; la cabeza is singular → duele.

turns.es: Hola, soy Laura. Trabajo en cardiología. ¿Y tú?

items.title: An older neighbor in the elevator

turns.es: Buenos días. ¿Usted vive en este edificio?
turns.en: Good morning. Do you live in this building?

opts: Sí, señora. Vivo en el tercer piso. ¿Y tú?
Sí, señora. Vivo en el tercer piso. ¿Y usted?
Sí, señora. Vives en el tercer piso. ¿Y usted?
turns.why: An older neighbor you don't know well → usted; about yourself → vivo.

turns.es: Yo vivo en el primer piso, con mi hija. No puedo subir escaleras porque me duelen las rodillas.
turns.en: I live on the first floor, with my daughter. I can't climb stairs because my knees hurt.

opts: Lo siento mucho. ¿Les duelen todos los días?
Lo siento mucho. ¿Te duelen todos los días?
Lo siento mucho. ¿Le duelen todos los días?
turns.why: Usted → le; the knees are plural → duelen. Les would mean 'them', and te is too informal.

turns.es: Sí, casi todos los días, sobre todo en la mañana.
turns.en: Yes, almost every day, especially in the morning.

turns.why: Sofía is a friend → te; one thing liked (la comida) → gusta.

turns.en: Do you want to have lunch with us today?

opts: Hoy no puedes, tengo que ver a un paciente a la una. ¿Mañana?
Hoy no puedo, tengo que ver a un paciente a la una. ¿Mañana?
Hoy no puedo, tengo ver a un paciente a la una. ¿Mañana?
turns.why: About yourself → puedo; 'have to' needs que: tengo que ver.

turns.en: Sure. What time do you usually have lunch?

opts: Normalmente almuerzo a las doce y media.
Normalmente almuerza a las doce y media.
Normalmente almorzo a las doce y media.

roleplay.title: New coworker at lunch
roleplay.setup: You're having lunch in the hospital cafeteria and a new nurse sits down next to you. Get to know her: where she lives, what she likes, and what she has to do this weekend.
roleplay.persona: You are Carmen Ruiz, 34, a cardiology nurse from Guadalajara, Mexico, who just started at the hospital. You live in Pilsen with your husband and two kids (8 and 11). You love cooking and salsa dancing; you don't like the Chicago cold. This Saturday you have to work, and on Sunday your kids play soccer in the park. Speak only in the present tense, in short, simple sentences, and use tú (you are coworkers). Use gustar/encantar, tener que, poder and querer naturally. Share details only when asked, and ask the learner a question back from time to time. If the learner makes a mistake, keep the conversation going and model the correct form in your reply.
roleplay.opening: ¡Hola! Soy Carmen, la nueva enfermera de cardiología. ¿Tú también trabajas en cardiología?
goals: Ask where she lives and how many kids she has
Find out two things she likes and one she doesn't (gustar/encantar)
Ask what she has to do this weekend (tener que)
Say one thing you like and one you don't, using también or tampoco
Ask at least three questions with different question words

roleplay.title: Neighbor in the elevator
roleplay.setup: You meet an older neighbor in your building's elevator. Use usted, chat about his routine and what he likes, and find out what is bothering him.
roleplay.persona: You are Don Ernesto Morales, 72, a retired carpenter from Michoacán, Mexico. You live on the second floor with your wife, Rosa. Your knees hurt, so you can't take the stairs; you walk in the park every morning anyway. You love baseball (the Cubs) and you don't like the cold. You can't drive at night because you don't see well, so your daughter drives you. This Thursday you have to go to the doctor. Speak only in the present tense, in simple sentences. Use usted with the learner and expect usted back; if the learner uses tú, smile and keep going but keep using usted yourself. Share details only when asked.
roleplay.opening: Buenos días. ¿Usted vive en el quinto piso?
goals: Use usted correctly throughout the conversation
Ask what he does in the mornings
Ask what he likes to do on weekends
Find out what he has to do this week (tener que)
